title: The Priestly Blessing
aka: the LORD bless you and keep you
lead: "May the LORD bless you and keep you" (Numbers 6:24–26) is the blessing Aaron's sons were told to speak over Israel. It is the oldest Bible text found in an ancient copy, and it is still spoken in synagogues and churches.

sections.b: Aaron blesses the people with raised hands at the first sacrifices (Leviticus 9:22), and Numbers 6:22–27 gives the words. The Psalms echo its lines (Psalm 4:6; Psalm 67:1; Psalm 80:3), and Sirach 50:20–21 describes the high priest Simon pronouncing it with the divine name in the temple. Two silver amulets from Ketef Hinnom in Jerusalem, from about 600 BC, carry forms of it. The Mishnah describes its daily use in the temple, and it is still given by descendants of Aaron in synagogues. Luke's Gospel ends with Jesus lifting his hands and blessing his disciples (Luke 24:50–51), and Christian churches use the words as a closing blessing.
